issues.description: This is three patches masquerading as one
issues.detail: The diff bundles a Risk Radar component, a 'Threat Score' -> 'ThreatScore' rename across unrelated files, a horizontal-bar-chart percentage refactor, and a generic filter-badge/labelFormatter refactor. These should be separate commits so each can be reviewed, reverted, and bisected on its own. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has two keys mapping to value 4
issues.detail: Adding `Info: 4` next to `Informational: 4` creates a silent duplicate ordering. If anything iterates SEVERITY_ORDER or reverse-maps value->key, you get nondeterministic behavior. Either normalize the input ('Info' -> 'Informational') at the boundary, or use a separate alias map. Don't smuggle aliases into an ordering table.

issues.description: getCategoryLabel heuristics will mislabel real category IDs
issues.detail: Removing the explicit CATEGORY_LABELS map and replacing it with 'short word == acronym' guesses means 'unused' stays 'Unused' (fine) but anything <=3 chars gets force-uppercased. 'e3'/'e5' worked before because they were in the table; now 'log' would become 'LOG', 'web' -> 'WEB'. The previous explicit table was correct code; the new heuristic is clever code. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: maxValue recomputed inside the render map for every bar
issues.detail: `Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value))` now runs once per bar inside the map callback. Hoist it above the loop. Small codebase, small data, but it's gratuitous O(n^2) where O(n) was right there.

issues.description: CategorySelector treats empty string and 'all' as the same sentinel
issues.detail: `if (value === '' || value === 'all')` — the Select only ever emits 'all' or a real categoryId. The empty-string branch is dead defensive code for a case that can't happen. Drop it; one sentinel, one check.

issues.description: Rename 'Threat Score' -> 'ThreatScore' is a product/branding change, not a code change
issues.detail: Burying a user-visible string rename across multiple files inside a 'Risk Radar' feature PR is how strings get reverted six months later because nobody knew the change was intentional. Split it out with its own commit message that says *why* the brand is now one word.

review.summary: The Risk Radar component itself is fine — it's a reasonable React feature with a sensible adapter extraction. The problem is the shape of the patch: it's at least three unrelated changes packed into one diff (radar feature, ThreatScore rename, bar-chart math refactor, generic labelFormatter plumbing). The category-label refactor replaces a correct explicit lookup table with heuristic guessing that will mislabel categories the first time someone adds 'log' or 'web', and SEVERITY_ORDER now has two keys mapping to the same rank, which is the kind of thing that bites you in a reverse lookup six months out. NEEDS-WORK: split the patch, kill the duplicate severity key, and either keep the explicit category map or document why heuristics are correct for every real category ID.
